metadata.description: A 3D wireframe cube with golden edges rotates on the Y-axis while scaling up, then rapidly expands and explodes into particles that fade away

components.name: RotatingCubePop
components.purpose: Main composition wrapper with background and 3D canvas

components.name: ThreeScene
components.purpose: 3D scene containing cube and particles, rendered inside ThreeCanvas

visibility.note: Cube fades out during explosion, fully gone by frame 72

components.name: ParticleField
components.purpose: Explosion particles that appear at frame 70

threeCanvasConfig.codeExample:
<ThreeCanvas
  width={width}
  height={height}
  camera={{ fov: 75, position: [0, 0, 470] }}
  style={{ backgroundColor: '#000000' }}
>
  {/* Scene content */}
</ThreeCanvas>

renderConfig.note: gl: 'angle' is REQUIRED for Three.js server-side rendering

timeline.description: Cube rotates continuously on Y-axis while smoothly scaling from small to large

implementation.note: Use fps from useVideoConfig() - do NOT hardcode
ALWAYS include both extrapolateLeft AND extrapolateRight

timeline.description: Cube rapidly scales up with overshoot effect, begins fading

easing.description: Ease-in-out-back for dramatic overshoot pop effect

timeline.description: Particles spawn from cube center and spread outward while fading

implementation.seedPattern: Use random(`particle-${property}-${index}`) for each particle property
implementation.critical: MUST use useMemo to prevent recalculation on every frame

implementation.note: Particles fade in quickly, then fade out as they spread

keyframes.description: End of smooth scale-up, begin pop

critical: MUST use random('unique-seed-string') from 'remotion' - NEVER Math.random()
MUST drive ALL animations from useCurrentFrame() return value
MUST use fps from useVideoConfig() for frame-rate-independent timing
MUST include BOTH extrapolateLeft: 'clamp' AND extrapolateRight: 'clamp' in interpolate()
MUST use layout='none' on any <Sequence> inside <ThreeCanvas>
MUST set chromiumOptions.gl = 'angle' in render config for Three.js
MUST NOT use CSS transitions, animations, or setTimeout/setInterval
MUST NOT use useState for animation values - derive everything from frame
recommended: SHOULD wrap geometry/material creation in useMemo() to prevent recreation each frame
SHOULD use <AbsoluteFill> for layering 2D content over 3D canvas
SHOULD extract animation logic into custom hooks for reusability
SHOULD use Easing.bezier() for smooth, professional-looking curves

memoizationPatterns.geometry: const geometry = useMemo(() => new BoxGeometry(size, size, size), [size]);
memoizationPatterns.particles: const particleData = useMemo(() => generateParticles(count, seed), [count, seed]);
memoizationPatterns.materials: const material = useMemo(() => new LineBasicMaterial({ color }), [color]);
memoizationPatterns.note: Memoize anything created with 'new' or expensive computations

sequenceUsage.note: Use Sequences to organize timeline phases, but MUST add layout='none' inside ThreeCanvas
sequenceUsage.example:
<ThreeCanvas width={width} height={height}>
  <Sequence from={0} durationInFrames={72} layout="none">
    <AnimatedCube />
  </Sequence>
  <Sequence from={70} layout="none">
    <ParticleField />
  </Sequence>
</ThreeCanvas>

antiPatterns.reason: useState causes non-deterministic renders across parallel threads
Math.random() gives different values per render thread, causing flicker
CSS transitions are time-based, not frame-based
Without clamping, values outside range can produce unexpected results

expectedBehavior: Frame 0: Cube visible at scale 0.3, rotation 0
Frame 30: Cube at approximately scale 0.9, rotated ~90 degrees
Frame 60: Cube at exactly scale 1.5, rotated ~180 degrees
Frame 70: Particles begin appearing, cube still visible but fading
Frame 72: Cube fully faded, particles spreading
Frame 90: Only particles visible, fully faded out
deterministicTests: Render frame 30 twice - pixel output must be identical
Render frame 70 on two threads simultaneously - particle positions must match
Render full video twice - file hash should be identical

flickeringParticles.symptom: Particles appear in different positions across frames
flickeringParticles.cause: Using Math.random() instead of deterministic random()

blackScreen.symptom: Three.js canvas renders black during export
blackScreen.solution: Add chromiumOptions: { gl: 'angle' } to render config

animationNotSmooth.cause: Using time-based animation instead of frame-based
animationNotSmooth.solution: Ensure all animations derive from useCurrentFrame(), not Date.now() or setTimeout

sequenceError.cause: Sequence components return a div by default
sequenceError.solution: Add layout="none" prop to all Sequences inside ThreeCanvas
